questions.q: What's the simplest question to ask when deciding between a calculated column and a measure?
options: Is the underlying data numeric or text?
Which one is faster to type?
Which table is the data currently in?
Do I need to slice/filter by this value, or just display a summarized number?
questions.explain: Filtering, grouping, and slicing require a column. Summarized, dynamically recalculated numbers require a measure.

questions.q: You need a customer 'High/Low value' category to use in a slicer. Which should you build?
options: Either works identically
A measure
Neither — this requires a Power Query step only
A calculated column
questions.explain: Slicers, legends, and axes need a filterable column. Measures can't be dragged into a slicer's field well.

questions.q: What happens if you build a calculated column for something that should have been a measure?
options: Power BI throws a clear error and prevents saving the column
It automatically converts itself into a measure
Nothing — the two are functionally interchangeable in every case
The value freezes at whatever it computed at refresh time, silently becoming wrong as filters change
questions.explain: A calculated column doesn't respond to report filters the way a measure does — it stays fixed until the next refresh, which can silently produce misleading numbers.

questions.q: What happens if you try to use a measure the way you'd use a column, e.g. dragging it into a slicer?
options: Power BI automatically creates a matching calculated column
The report crashes
It doesn't work — measures aren't filterable, only summarizable
It works exactly like a column would
questions.explain: Measures exist to be aggregated and displayed, not filtered by — you simply can't use one where a filterable column is required.

questions.q: Which scenario calls for a measure rather than a calculated column?
options: Adding a column that concatenates first and last name
Creating a combined City, State field to plot on a map
Showing this year's sales as a percentage of last year's, recalculating as filters change
Categorizing products into price tiers to filter by
questions.explain: A dynamically recalculated ratio that responds to whatever filters are applied is exactly what a measure is for — the other three examples are all filterable categories, which need calculated columns.
